forecast-period.text: A trough and cold front over western SA will track eastwards across the rest of SA on Friday before a weak high briefly establishes in the north on Saturday. Another series of troughs and cold fronts are expected to enter western SA early on Sunday, crossing the state then clearing in the east by the end of Monday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Showers and thunderstorms moving across central and western SA, reaching eastern districts in the late afternoon and clearing from the west later during the day. Thunderstorms may become severe across parts of the pastorals and central districts bringing damaging wind gusts, large hail and a slight chance of heavy rainfall. Maximum temperatures near to above average in the east, grading to below average in the west. Northeast to northwesterly winds, ahead of a fresh and gusty west to southwesterly change extending across the state throughout the day.

Isolated light showers about the southern agricultural areas, mostly clearing by the afternoon. Isolated thunderstorms possible early across the far north and northeast. Maximum temperatures below average. Light and variable winds in the north, tending west to southwesterly winds across the south.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing across the north and west, extending into central and eastern districts during the late afternoon and evening and becoming more scattered. Severe thunderstorms bringing damaging wind gusts possible over parts of the west. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh at times in the north with a south to southwesterly change moving into the far west during the afternoon.

text.p: Scattered showers and thunderstorms across central and eastern districts during the morning and afternoon, isolated in the west. Thunderstorms contracting to the north in the late afternoon. Maximum temperatures below average in the east, grading to well below average in the west. North to northwesterly winds in the far north ahead of moderate west to southwesterly change extending throughout, freshening near the coast.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: Broadly 2 to 10 mm across the pastoral districts, increasing to 5 to 15 mm over the northern agricultural areas and 10 to 20 mm across the southern agricultural areas. Isolated higher falls of 20 to 30 mm possible across southern parts of the peninsulas, Kangaroo Island and the Mouth Lofty Ranges. Localised falls of 30 to 40 mm possible with severe thunderstorms.
